findings: smoothingSegment_subsegment_data applies the proved original-successor parameter construction to the actual selectedMarkPerm slot. Its parameter t lies strictly above that slot's actual half-open parameter s and at most one; neither t nor positivity is supplied.

selectedMarkPerm_evaluation identifies the starting physical point with the selected slot's edgePoint. At a selected crossing this uses equal geometric crossing evaluations while keeping the two incoming marks distinct. No zero segment joining the twin marks is inserted.

The ending physical point is the actual smoothingSuccessor evaluation by the constructed composition of selectedMarkPerm and markSuccessor. The affine identity then gives the exact formula edgePoint(s+u*(t-s)) for every real u.

Positive direction uses the exact scalar c=t-s with c>0 and the actual original oriented edge. G1 supplies that edge's nonzero vector, so scalar multiplication gives genuinely nonzero endpoint displacement.

Positive length uses euclideanLength from the canonical EuclideanPlane module, defined through the complex-plane norm with the proved square-root coordinate formula. It does not accidentally use the product-space max norm on Plane=ℝ×ℝ.

Containment is explicitly restricted to 0≤u≤1. Nonnegative s and nonnegative u*(t-s) give the lower parameter bound; u≤1 and t≤1 give the upper bound. The formula witnesses membership in the actual original edgeSegment.

Injectivity is local to each single smoothingSegment as a function of its real interpolation parameter. It follows from injectivity of edgePoint on a proved nonzero edge and cancellation of the strictly positive parameter gap; no entire carrier curve is asserted injective.
